title: Columbus disaster
summary: An Aeromarine Airways aircraft operating a flight from Key West to Havana was forced to land in the Straits of Florida on 13 January 1923. The aircraft foundered, resulting in 4 fatalities, marking the first fatal airline accident in the United States.

title: East Malling air disaster
summary: The aircraft suffered a starboard engine failure during cruise, forcing an attempt at emergency landing with severely limited single-engine performance. Miscommunication between the mechanic and passengers resulted in four passengers moving toward the rear of the aircraft, significantly affecting the center of gravity. The aircraft entered an uncontrollable spin and crashed at East Malling, killing one passenger and injuring nine others.
probable_cause: The starboard engine failure created a hazardous situation that the aircraft's single-engine performance could not manage; the subsequent shift in weight and balance when passengers moved to the rear of the aircraft rendered the aircraft uncontrollable and initiated a spin.

events.text: About 45 minutes after take-off from Lympne, the starboard engine failed as the aircraft flew at about 65 kn at an altitude of just under 2000 ft.
The pilot altered course, intending to land at either Marden or Penshurst.
The mechanic asked two passengers to move towards the rear of the aircraft.
Four passengers moved towards the rear of the aircraft, which affected the centre of gravity and caused the aircraft to enter into a spin.
The aircraft crashed at East Malling with no fire, and the aircraft was written off.
